metadata.description: YouthTempo starts with everyday rhythms, helping young people understand how they are doing, express their feelings, and connect with trusted support more easily.

footer.description: Young people can check in with how they are doing and make sense of their feelings. With permission, parents and teachers can understand changes and help connect them with the right support when needed.

metadata.title: YouthTempo | Earlier Support for Young People

hero.label: Everyday mental health support for young people
hero.title: How have you been lately?
hero.description: Start with sleep, meals, movement, daily tasks, and emotions. Check in with how things have been, so it is easier to explain what you need to someone you trust.
hero.imageAlt: A young person moving forward at their own pace, supported by parents, teachers, and professionals

demo.title: Choose what feels closest and see a simple summary
demo.description: Try it here without saving anything. After you choose, you will see a brief summary and one small step you can try right away.

panel.question: How did it feel to get your day started this morning?

steady.label: Going fairly well
steady.summary: Your rhythm felt fairly steady this morning.
steady.step: Keep doing what is already helping. You do not need to add another task.

slow.label: A bit difficult
slow.summary: Getting started felt difficult this morning. Notice it without blaming yourself.
slow.step: Begin with the smallest thing, such as getting ready, drinking some water, or packing your bag.

stuck.label: Very hard to start
stuck.summary: It was very hard to get started this morning. Sleep or stress may be affecting you too.
stuck.step: Reduce what you need to do to one step, or tell an adult you trust.

dailyChanges.label: Why start with everyday life
dailyChanges.title: Changes often show up in daily life first
dailyChanges.description: Poor sleep, loss of appetite, less movement, or difficulty starting schoolwork can appear before someone can say, “I feel stressed.” Noticing these changes can help you decide whether you need rest, a conversation, or more support.

audiences.label: Find the right place to begin
audiences.title: Start from where you are
audiences.description: Young people can check in and express themselves. Parents can understand and support. Teachers can notice changes and connect young people with support when needed.

teens.title: I am a young person
teens.label: Check in and express yourself
teens.text: Look at today's rhythms and make sense of feelings that are hard to explain. You can also write something for yourself or an adult you trust.

parents.title: I am a parent
parents.label: Understand what has been happening
parents.text: Look at recent changes in your child's sleep, meals, movement, and learning, then find a gentler way to start a conversation.

teachers.title: I am a teacher
teachers.label: Notice changes
teachers.text: See broader changes among the students you support, understand individual situations when needed, and connect with families or professional support.

support.label: From check-in to support
support.title: Take it one step at a time
support.description: Start with what daily life has been like, then make sense of how you feel. If it is too much to manage alone, ask someone you trust to think it through with you.

daily.title: Start with everyday life
daily.label: Sleep, meals, movement, and learning
daily.text: You do not have to explain everything at once. Begin with the most noticeable change from the past few days.

feelings.title: Put your feelings into words
feelings.label: Emotions and stress
feelings.text: Choose a few emotion words that feel close, or write down worries that keep coming back.

people.title: Ask someone to help when needed
people.label: Family, teachers, or professional support
people.text: If it feels too hard to cope alone, tell someone you trust what has been happening and decide together who to contact next.

principles.label: Our approach
principles.title: A check-in helps explain what is happening. It does not define anyone.

items.one: 1. One check-in will never be used to define you
items.two: 2. Summaries only organize what you have shared
items.three: 3. When needed, we will encourage you to contact someone you trust

hero.title: Your space
hero.description: Start here to check in with how you have been, work through something on your mind, or write down what feels hard to say face to face.
hero.imageAlt: A student holding a notebook, ready to check in at her own pace

rhythm.alt: An everyday rhythm made up of sleep, waking, meals, movement, and task engagement

mood.title: I am not sure how to describe my feelings
mood.text: You do not have to explain everything yet. Choose a few emotion words that feel close, then add what happened when you are ready.
mood.alt: A mood map made up of different colors

worry.title: My mind gets busy at bedtime
worry.text: Write down your worries and separate what you can act on from what can wait for now.

referral.title: I want to know what I can do next
referral.text: If stress continues for many days or is clearly affecting daily life or learning, explore the kinds of support that may fit.

youngAdults.title: Are you 18 or older and want to use YouthTempo independently?
youngAdults.description: Young adults aged 18–25 can provide their own informed consent. No school or guardian needs to join.

support.title: Has it been hard to cope lately?
support.description: Start by talking with an adult or teacher you trust, or explore support options that may fit.

feedback.title: Is there anything you would change?
feedback.description: Take two minutes to tell us what worked well and where you got stuck.

hero.label: For parents
hero.title: Parent space
hero.description: Start by noticing recent changes in your child's sleep, meals, and movement, then find a way to talk that feels open and free from blame.
hero.imageAlt: A parent listening calmly and ready to support their child

intro.visibleText: You can only view records for a child whose connection to you has been confirmed by the school. You cannot see information about other students. One check-in never tells the whole story; use it to understand what has been happening and begin a conversation.
intro.concreteTitle: Start with specific changes before asking why
intro.concreteText: Many young people find it hard to answer, “What is wrong?” Start instead with something specific, such as poor sleep, difficulty getting up, or finding it hard to begin schoolwork.

starts.title: Where can parents begin?
starts.description: Choose the most specific starting point and the one least likely to create conflict.

daily.title: Look at everyday life first
daily.text: Start with sleep, waking, meals, movement, and learning. Notice whether any changes have continued over time.
daily.alt: A father and daughter looking together at the five SWEET areas of everyday rhythm

listen.title: Help them feel less defensive
listen.text: Focus on understanding how your child is doing, rather than judging, pressing for reasons, or asking for immediate change.
listen.alt: A parent setting judgment aside and listening quietly to their child

conversation.title: Find an easier way to begin
conversation.text: Say what you have noticed and why you care, then choose a time when you can talk without interruptions.
conversation.alt: A parent and child building a safe conversation step by step

support.title: Connect with support when needed
support.text: If the situation continues to affect daily life and learning, bring together support from family, school, and professionals.
support.alt: A parent connecting their child with school and professional support

messages.title: Read private messages from your child
messages.description: Messages your child chooses to share with you appear together on a dedicated page.

feedback.title: How did YouthTempo work for you?
feedback.description: Take two minutes to tell us what helped and what could be improved.

sweet.title: SWEET: what parents can notice
sweet.description: SWEET organizes daily life into five observable areas. Changes do not necessarily mean something serious is wrong, but if they continue, it is worth checking in with your child.

sleep.title: Sleep
sleep.question: Has sleep been fairly steady?
sleep.text: Notice whether bedtime, waking during the night, or morning tiredness is clearly different from before.

wake.title: Wake up on time
wake.question: Is it difficult to get started in the morning?
wake.text: Notice whether getting up, getting ready, leaving home, or beginning the day has become harder.

eat.title: Eat healthily
eat.question: Are meals regular?
eat.text: Look for noticeable changes in energy, frequent loss of appetite, skipped meals, or relying on snacks to get through the day.

exercise.title: Exercise
exercise.question: Has physical activity decreased noticeably?
exercise.text: Notice whether your child is going out, moving, or taking part in familiar activities less often.

task.title: Task engagement
task.question: Is it difficult to start schoolwork or everyday tasks?
task.text: Look beyond outcomes and notice whether starting and staying with a task has become harder.

aidet.title: AIDET: a way for parents to begin the conversation
aidet.description: AIDET breaks a conversation into five steps. You do not need to use the terminology—just follow the order to express your care clearly.

acknowledge.label: Acknowledge how your child may feel
acknowledge.example: I know you may be really tired lately, and that you are not putting things off on purpose.

introduce.label: Explain why you are here
introduce.example: I am not here to tell you off. I just want to understand how you have been lately.

duration.label: Keep the conversation brief
duration.example: Let's talk for ten minutes. We do not have to solve everything right now.

explanation.label: Explain why everyday rhythms matter
explanation.example: Sleep, waking, meals, and movement can affect emotions and attention. I want to see if there is one place where I can make things a little easier for you.

thankYou.label: Thank your child for sharing
thankYou.example: Thank you for telling me. I know this may not be easy to talk about.

conversation.title: Ways to start the conversation
conversation.description: You do not need to repeat these word for word. Choose one that sounds like you and use it to begin.

phrases.one: Have you been feeling a bit tired lately? I would like to listen.
phrases.two: Let's talk for ten minutes. We do not need to solve it now.
phrases.three: It is okay if you are not sure how to explain it yet.
phrases.four: I will listen without judging. What has felt most difficult lately?

furtherSupport.title: When to seek further support
furtherSupport.label: Connect with more support
furtherSupport.text: If stress continues, or sleep, learning, relationships, or daily life are clearly affected, families can consider a school counsellor or qualified mental health professional, and medical or emergency services when necessary. This is not about blaming anyone. The goal is to help your child access support that fits their needs.

oneThing.title: One thing parents can do first
oneThing.text: Begin with one specific change, such as poor sleep, difficulty getting up, or finding it hard to start schoolwork. Explain that you simply want to understand what has been happening, then listen to what your child says.

resources.title: Family–school support guide
resources.text: Practical guidance for parents and teachers to understand young people's rhythms, feelings, and support needs earlier.

hero.label: For teachers
hero.title: Teacher workspace
hero.description: Start by looking for ongoing changes among the students you support. When needed, review the details and decide together with the student whether to involve family or connect with further support.
hero.imageAlt: A teacher holding a notebook, ready to listen to a student

week.title: Start with the past week
week.description: See which students have recent records and whether any changes in their daily rhythms have continued.
week.alt: A teacher reviewing an overview of recent changes among the students they support

details.title: Then look at the details
details.description: When needed, review a student's recent summaries and their own records, then use specific changes to begin a conversation.
details.alt: A teacher and student reviewing the five SWEET areas of everyday rhythm together

listen.title: Hear what students want to say
listen.description: Read messages that students chose to write to a teacher when they found them difficult to say face to face.
listen.alt: A teacher reading a private message from a student

conversation.title: Use the record to start a conversation
conversation.text: When changes in sleep, eating, movement, or task engagement continue, you might begin with: “Has something been leaving you especially tired lately?” Listen first, then decide together whether more support is needed.

feedback.title: What could work better?
feedback.description: Take two minutes to share how the platform worked in practice and help us improve the pilot.

hero.label: For ages 18–25
hero.title: You do not have to wait for life to feel settled before caring for your rhythm.
hero.description: Leaving school, starting university, or entering work can bring more freedom—and make daily life easier to lose track of. You can use YouthTempo independently, without a school or guardian joining.
hero.imageAlt: A path of growth moving forward step by step at your own rhythm

tools.title: Start with what you need most right now
tools.description: Choose one thing at a time. This does not need to become another to-do list.

rhythm.title: Look at your recent rhythm
rhythm.text: Start with sleep, waking, meals, movement, and the tasks in front of you. You do not need to understand every problem first.
rhythm.alt: A check-in path made up of five everyday rhythm areas

mood.title: Put complicated feelings into words
mood.text: When emotions feel mixed, choose the feelings that come closest, then add what has just happened.
mood.alt: A mood map made up of different colors

worry.title: Set worries aside before sleep
worry.text: Separate what you can act on from what cannot be addressed yet. You do not have to solve everything tonight.
worry.alt: Setting worries aside for now under the moonlight

support.title: Know who to reach out to for support
support.text: If the situation continues to affect study, work, or daily life, find support that matches the level of urgency.
support.alt: A step-by-step path to the right support

confirmation.label: Independent consent
confirmation.title: If you are 18 or older, you can consent for yourself
confirmation.text: After signing in, select “I am 18 or older,” read the data information, and confirm. Guardian consent and school membership are not required.

records.label: Your records
records.title: Only you can see them by default
records.text: If you have not joined a school, the school and its teachers cannot view your records. You can export your data, delete individual records, or close your account.

boundary.label: What YouthTempo is for
boundary.title: It is not a diagnostic or emergency service
boundary.text: If you are in immediate danger of harming yourself or someone else, contact local emergency services, the police, or someone nearby who can come to you now.

teens.title: Are you aged 14–18 and part of the school pilot?
teens.description: The youth space includes support connections with parents, teachers, and schools.

hero.title: The SWEET model
hero.description: YouthTempo begins with everyday rhythms to make earlier support more accessible for young people.
hero.imageAlt: A cycle of everyday rhythms made up of sleep, waking, meals, movement, and task engagement

modules.title: Five areas of everyday rhythm
modules.description: Together, these areas help young people, families, and schools understand changes more clearly and offer support before challenges become more serious.

sleep.title: Sleep
sleep.question: How long did you sleep last night, and how restful was it?
sleep.summary: Sleep supports emotional steadiness, attention, and physical recovery.
sleep.example: Sleep check-ins, making sense of emotions before bed, and helpful sleep habit reminders.

wake.title: Wake
wake.question: When you woke today, did you feel tired, calm, or tense?
wake.summary: How the day begins can affect a young person's emotions, focus, and ability to get going.
wake.example: Morning check-ins, gentle waking suggestions, and ways to make sense of the morning.

eat.title: Eat
eat.question: Have you eaten regularly today?
eat.summary: Regular meals help keep energy steadier and make everyday activities easier to maintain.
eat.example: Meal-rhythm check-ins and practical wellbeing reminders.

exercise.title: Exercise
exercise.question: Have you had any light physical activity today?
exercise.summary: Gentle movement can ease stress and help the body and emotions feel less stuck.
exercise.example: Light-activity check-ins and low-pressure movement challenges.

task.title: Task engagement
task.question: Were you able to manage basic learning or everyday tasks today?
task.summary: Task engagement can show whether learning, daily life, and social participation are continuing steadily.
task.example: Tracking study pressure, breaking tasks into steps, and noticing progress.

hero.title: Privacy & safety
hero.description: We retain only the information needed to provide the service and limit access to records according to each user's role.

principles.title: How you can manage your information
principles.description: This page explains what may be retained, who can see it, and what you can do if you need help or want to delete your data.

noLabels.title: No labels
noLabels.text: YouthTempo records everyday rhythms and support needs. It does not reduce young people to being “fine” or “a problem.”

minimum.title: Only what is needed
minimum.text: We retain only the information needed to complete records and provide the service. We do not collect unrelated personal information.

safety.title: Safety comes first
safety.text: When someone describes a clear danger or cannot confirm that they are safe, YouthTempo prioritizes guidance to contact a trusted adult, the school, or emergency services.

control.title: You can manage your information
control.text: After signing in, you can view, download, or delete your own content. Each role can only see records they are authorized to access.

community.title: Community safety and reporting for minors
community.description: Community rules apply to posts and replies. A reporter's identity is not shared with the content author, and content with a greater potential for harm is reviewed sooner.

urgent.title: Urgent priority · 2-hour target
urgent.text: Clear immediate danger, encouragement of self-harm or suicide, and sexual content or abuse involving minors enter the urgent queue. If someone is in danger, do not wait for the platform to respond. Contact a trusted adult immediately and call 110 or 120.

high.title: Priority review · 24-hour target
high.text: Bullying, abuse, threats, disclosure of personal information, and other clearly dangerous or inappropriate content receive priority review. Depending on the situation, content may be hidden, accounts restricted, or necessary records retained.

standard.title: Standard review · 72-hour target
standard.text: Fraud, advertising, spam, and other rule violations enter the standard queue. Complex cases may take longer than the initial-review target to investigate, and updates appear under My report status in the community.

community.legalPrefix: The 2-, 24-, and 72-hour targets above are the times we aim to meet for an initial review; they are not uniform legal deadlines. If someone is in danger, do not wait for a community response. The community rules are informed by

account.title: Sign-in and data retention
account.description: Individual users can view their own records. School roles access records according to school membership and student assignments. Parents can only view records for children whose connection to them has been confirmed by the school.

email.title: Email sign-in
email.text: Sign in with a verification code sent to your email. You do not need to create or remember a password.

records.title: Saving records
records.text: SWEET records that you choose to save after signing in are added to your personal history.

school.title: School access
school.text: School leads can view records for students at their school. Support teachers can only view students assigned to them by the school.

delete.title: Deleting records
delete.text: Students can delete their own saved SWEET records under Account.

export.title: Exporting data and closing an account
export.text: After signing in, you can immediately download a copy of your data or permanently close your account. YouthTempo does not retain exported files.

consent.title: Informed consent for minors and guardians
consent.description: The current YouthTempo pilot is for students aged 14–18. Students need clear information about how their data is used, and students aged 14–17 in the school pilot also need confirmation from a verified guardian.

student.title: The student confirms first
student.text: Students read about the data covered, how it is used, which roles can see it, and how to withdraw. They select only an age range and do not provide an exact date of birth.

guardian.title: The guardian then confirms
guardian.text: For students aged 14–17 in the school pilot, a guardian whose connection has been confirmed by the school completes the confirmation in their own account.

summary.title: Confirm again before generating a summary
summary.text: Before a summary is generated, users are reminded that their responses may include sensitive information about daily life and health, and must actively select the consent checkbox.

withdraw.title: Consent can be withdrawn
withdraw.text: Students or guardians can withdraw consent from the Account page. After withdrawal, the student cannot save new records, send messages, or post in the community.

coverage.title: What the consent covers
coverage.text: Account details, SWEET everyday-rhythm responses, AI-generated summaries, private messages, community posts, and the relationship information needed to limit access for schools, teachers, and guardians. Users are not asked for a national identity number or exact date of birth.

afterWithdrawal.title: What happens after withdrawal
afterWithdrawal.text: After consent is withdrawn, no new records can be saved and no new messages or community posts can be sent. Existing content can still be viewed, downloaded, or deleted individually, and the account can be closed to delete associated data.

consent.legalPrefix: When personal information is processed on the basis of consent, the law requires consent to be informed, voluntary, explicit, and easy to withdraw. Separate consent is required for sensitive personal information such as medical and health information, and guardian consent is required for the personal information of children under 14. YouthTempo's requirement that both students aged 14–17 and their guardians confirm participation in the school pilot is an additional safeguard. See

retention.title: Data export, account closure, and retention periods
retention.description: Users can exercise these rights directly in account settings without first contacting the school or platform or giving a reason. An export contains only the current account's data; it does not include private records belonging to linked children, students, or other users.

active.title: While an account remains active
active.text: While the account is active, data is retained only to provide the service, show the user's history, and meet safety responsibilities. Users can delete individual SWEET records or close their account at any time.

deletion.title: Account closure takes effect immediately
deletion.text: Once account closure is confirmed, the account and associated personal data are deleted immediately. YouthTempo does not separately retain downloaded copies of the data.

audit.title: Safety handling records · up to 24 months
audit.text: Safety handling records that do not contain plain-text email addresses or user identifiers may be retained for up to 24 months to review safety issues and confirm that deletion has been completed. They are cleared when the retention period ends.

backups.title: Backup copies
backups.text: The specific retention period for backup copies is still being confirmed and will be published on this page when available. Registered deletion requests will still be applied when services are restored from a backup.

deletionScope.title: What account closure deletes
deletionScope.text: Account details, SWEET records, messages, school and guardian relationships, consent records, WeChat links, personal community content, and reports are deleted with the account. Community moderation actions involving the account retain only de-identified safety records.

retention.legalPrefix: The Personal Information Protection Law provides rights to access and copy personal information and to request deletion in circumstances including when the processing purpose has been achieved, the service has ended, the retention period has expired, or consent has been withdrawn. The Regulations on Network Data Security Management require accessible ways to copy or delete data, restrict processing, close an account, and withdraw consent. See

schoolExit.title: Data handling when a school leaves the pilot
schoolExit.description: After a school leaves, it can no longer access information about the students involved. Student and parent accounts are not closed as a result.

access.title: School access ends immediately
access.text: When withdrawal takes effect, school leads, teachers, and other school roles immediately lose access to the school space, student records, and support relationships.

personal.title: Personal accounts remain active
personal.text: Student, parent, and teacher accounts are not deleted because a school leaves. Individuals can continue to view or export their own data or close their account.

relationships.title: School relationships are removed
relationships.text: School memberships, teacher–student relationships, parent–child relationships, and pending invitations are removed. School affiliation is removed from personal SWEET records, messages, and consent records.

notes.title: School collaboration data is deleted
notes.text: Follow-up notes created only for school collaboration are deleted when the school leaves. Exit-operation records that do not contain student content may be retained for up to 24 months.

schoolExit.legalPrefix: After a school leaves, school leads and teachers can no longer access student information through their previous school relationships. Individuals can still exercise their legal rights to access, copy, or delete their data or close their account. For details, see

rules.label: Community rules for minors
rules.title: Protect people first, then discuss the issue
rules.description: These rules apply to posts and replies. When content may harm someone, we aim to review it promptly and may hide it, restrict posting, or report it as required by law, depending on the situation.

respect.title: Be respectful—no bullying
respect.text: Do not insult, threaten, defame, gang up on, or deliberately damage someone's reputation. Express disagreements clearly and kindly.

privacy.title: Protect yourself and others
privacy.text: Do not share real names, school or class details, home addresses, contact details, account information, locations, or private experiences or images without consent.

harm.title: Do not share dangerous content
harm.text: Do not post sexual, violent, gambling-related, or illegal content. Do not encourage self-harm or suicide or invite others to imitate unsafe behaviour.

authentic.title: Be genuine and non-commercial
authentic.text: Do not impersonate a professional, commit fraud, ask for money, share suspicious links, post repeatedly, or use the community for marketing.

targets.urgent: Urgent priority: initial review target within 2 hours
targets.high: Bullying, privacy, and similar concerns: initial review target within 24 hours
targets.standard: Other rule violations: initial review target within 72 hours

rules.targetDisclaimer: These are targets for an initial review, not emergency-response times. If someone is in immediate danger, do not wait for a community response. Contact a trusted adult and call 110 or 120.

compose.placeholder: You do not need to explain everything perfectly. Start with what you most want the other person to understand.
compose.anonymousDescription: Keep this anonymous to the teacher. Only an authorized school lead can identify the sender if the message describes a clear safety concern.
